_comment: Runtime config for the DoseRAD2026 algorithm container. Lives in the model tarball so
parameters change with a ~9 MB re-upload instead of an 18.7 GB image rebuild.
Precedence: built-in default < this file < environment variable.
MEASURED IN THE CONTAINER 2026-08-07 (eager, no padding, 3 invokes each, HTTP checked):
items=4 -> 10.07 GiB reserved, steady invoke 7.29 s
items=6 -> 14.15 GiB reserved, steady invoke 7.00 s   <- shipped
items=8 -> HTTP 500, 'CUDA driver error: device not ready' on a 16 GB card.
Memory scales ~2.04 GiB per item, so items=8 projects to ~18.2 GiB: it should fit a
24 GB A10G, but the observed failure mode is a hard CUDA fault, not the graceful
dense-batch shrink -- oom_shrinks was 0. Not worth the risk for the ~0.3 s items=6
already banks. Larger batches ARE faster; 4 is not the safe default it looked like.
compile_correction_model: FALSE deliberately. With it on, the correction model
recompiles inside the metered /invoke -- the synthetic warmup allocates its tensors
outside inference_mode, so the 'energy' tensor dispatch key set mismatches the real
call and the guard fails (confirmed via TORCH_LOGS=recompiles). Measured cost: health
93 s + first invoke 84.9 s against 9 s / 9.1 s eager. Do not enable until a container
run shows warmup followed by a first invoke at steady-state speed.
pad_inference_batch: FALSE -- it exists only to keep one batch shape for compile, and
with compile off it just pads the tail chunk with wasted rows.
